fake_rule: true while any layer source in layers.json contains FAKE (same as plan.json inputs_fake)

layout.order: row-major inside each tile, row 0 = north edge, index = row * tile_width + col
layout.window_cell_of_point: col = floor((x - origin_x) / cell_m), row = height - 1 - floor((y - origin_y) / cell_m)
layout.window_cell_centre: x = origin_x + (col + 0.5) * cell_m, y = origin_y + (height - row - 0.5) * cell_m
layout.tile_of_cell: the tile whose row0 <= row < row0 + shape[0] and col0 <= col < col0 + shape[1]
layout.nearest_safe: two uint16 per cell: [2 * i] = row, [2 * i + 1] = col, in WINDOW rows/cols (not tile rows/cols)
layout.search_bound: paths never leave the window: the browser only searches inside it

nearest_safe.meaning: row, col of the nearest safe cell, window rows/cols

nearest_safe_dist.meaning: m, cell centre to cell centre

risk_rate.meaning: risk-min per min walked, 0 where blocked

safety_codes.name: safe
safety_codes.text: safe: the pad passes every rule

safety_codes.name: marginal
safety_codes.text: marginal: passes, but within 20% of at least one limit

safety_codes.name: outside_coverage
safety_codes.text: outside coverage: the 30 m circle around this point does not fit inside the data

safety_codes.name: no_data
safety_codes.text: no data: a pad cell has no DEM or slope value

safety_codes.name: hazard_or_clearance
safety_codes.text: hazard: a pad cell is not green or cannot be walked on, or a red, over-limit-slope or cliff-buffer cell is within 30 m

safety_codes.name: too_steep
safety_codes.text: too steep: the pad tilts more than 5 deg

safety_codes.name: height_range
safety_codes.text: height range: more than 1 m between the highest and lowest point once the tilt is removed

safety_codes.name: too_rough
safety_codes.text: too rough: more than 0.25 m RMS about the pad's best-fit plane

safety_order: the lowest failure code wins: outside_coverage > no_data > hazard_or_clearance > too_steep > height_range > too_rough
landing_rule: a click on a safe (0) or marginal (1) cell stays where it is; any other click moves to the centre of nearest_safe, a straight-line move (the lander comes down from above)

pad_radius_m.source: Team assumption (Tushaar), pending Nahla: radius of the circular lander pad that must be safe

max_pad_slope_deg.source: Team assumption (Tushaar), pending Nahla: tilt of the best-fit plane through the pad's DEM cells

max_roughness_m.unit: m (RMS of the DEM about the pad's best-fit plane)
max_roughness_m.source: Team assumption (Tushaar), pending Nahla: half of the yellow (careful) roughness of 0.5 m in terrain/thresholds.toml [roughness], so a pad is clearly smoother than ground that is only walkable with care. Scale differs: terrain measures RMS about the local mean in a 5 x 5 cell (25 m) window on the 5 m grid; this is RMS about a plane over the whole pad (50 m across) on the same grid

max_height_range_m.unit: m (highest minus lowest DEM cell on the pad, after removing the best-fit plane)
max_height_range_m.source: Team assumption (Tushaar), pending Nahla: catches a single step, mound or pit that the RMS roughness averages away; not a sourced lander clearance

hazard_clearance_m.source: Team assumption (Tushaar), pending Nahla: no red cell, over-limit slope cell or cliff-buffer cell this close to the pad centre

marginal_pct.source: Team assumption (Tushaar): a pad that passes but is within this share of any limit is marked marginal

ti_warn_below.source: terrain/thresholds.toml [thermal_inertia] yellow_below (loose sand; terrain's starting value, not checked against Jezero data). Used only for a warning flag, never a hard rule, and only while layers.json marks the thermal layer as real

roughness_source: computed from dem.tif: RMS about the best-fit plane over the pad
roughness_note: Scale caveat: terrain's roughness (terrain/thresholds.toml [roughness], terrain/hazard_map.py) is the RMS about the local mean in a 5 x 5 cell (25 m) window on the 5 m grid; the older terrain/hazards pipeline (terrain/config/hazards.yaml) used a 5 m window on 1 m data. Ours is the RMS about one best-fit plane over the whole pad (50 m across) on the 5 m grid, so the numbers are not directly comparable. The limit is a team assumption pending Nahla.
height_range_note: landing.max_height_range_m (1.0 m by default) is a team assumption, not a sourced lander clearance: the highest minus the lowest pad cell after removing the best-fit plane.

mask_codes.name: buffer
mask_codes.text: inside the 5 m buffer around over-limit slopes

mask_codes.name: walled_off
mask_codes.text: passable, but walled off from the start by blocked cells

mask_note: codes 1-5 are stored; 0 reachable and 6 walled off are results of a search, never stored

edge_rule.neighbours: 8 (search.connectivity); a neighbour outside the window or with mask != 0 is never entered
edge_rule.step_length_m: straight: cell_m; diagonal: sqrt(cell_m * cell_m + cell_m * cell_m)
edge_rule.planning_rate: p = time_rate * (1 + w * risk_rate), float64, in that order
edge_rule.step_cost: L * (p_from + p_to) / 2, float64, in that order
edge_rule.update: relax a neighbour only when g + step_cost < its current g (strictly less)
edge_rule.totals: along the found path, from the landing cell, summed in path order in float64: distance_m += step_m; walk_min += step_m * (time_rate_a + time_rate_b) / 2; risk_min += step_m * (time_rate_a * risk_rate_a + time_rate_b * risk_rate_b) / 2; where step_m is cell_m straight and cell_m * sqrt(2) diagonal
edge_rule.sealed_gaps: already closed in the mask (cost.py), so no corner check is needed

budget.rule: one way only: needed_min = walk_min + ingress_min + stop_min; over budget when needed_min > usable_min, i.e. when walk_min > walk_limit_min. No return walk is counted.
